author: Agence France-Presse
description:
The European Union will from Sunday slap a €2 (US$2.25) handling fee on packages from outside the 27-nation bloc in a bid to curb the influx from China.
The new levy – coming just weeks before the Black Friday, Cyber Monday and Christmas season shopping rushes – will be on top of the EU’s €3 fee on small parcels.
The fee will apply to each type of item in a package sent directly to consumers from outside the EU regardless of the parcel’s value.
For example, if there are 10 T-shirts in a package,...
title: New levy on non-EU parcels kicks in on Sunday in a bid to curb the influx from China

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s re-election preserves Beijing’s most critical foothold in Latin America, while positioning Brasilia to leverage the US-China rivalry over its vast rare earth reserves without picking sides.
Lula, 80, secured an unprecedented fourth term on Sunday after winning 51.8 per cent of the run-off vote to defeat right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro. The son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro and Trump ally has, however, refused to concede.
Beijing...
title: Win for Lula boosts China’s foothold and gives Brazil rare earths leverage

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
China may have begun limited production of its next-generation KJ-3000 airborne early warning aircraft, with satellite imagery suggesting that three possible production examples were already parked at a factory as early as April, according to an imagery analyst.
If brought into service, the aircraft could help the People’s Liberation Army to detect threats, track targets and coordinate air operations across the western Pacific, including during a potential conflict over Taiwan involving US and...
title: China’s next-generation KJ-3000 radar planes may have quietly entered production

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Former Japanese prime minister Yasuo Fukuda, who championed closer ties with China during his brief tenure and later served as a crucial diplomatic intermediary during bilateral crises, has died at the age of 90.
Fukuda died of heart failure on Thursday at a Tokyo hospital, Japanese media reported on Monday. His passing came as the relationship he spent decades nurturing faces its gravest test since diplomatic normalisation in 1972.
Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun offered...
title: Death of former PM Yasuo Fukuda leaves void in fraught China-Japan relations

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth will travel to the Philippines this week to meet regional allies, the Pentagon announced on Sunday.
The visit comes amid a push by Washington to tighten security ties in the Indo-Pacific ahead of an expected meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in southern China.
Hegseth, a former Fox News host, has faced criticism from Democrats and some Republicans over his handling of the war against Iran, as well as concerns that the conflict could divert...
title: Pentagon chief Hegseth to visit Philippines to meet US allies at Asean events

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese researchers have created a new model to convert satellite surface elevation data for the Greenland Ice Sheet into a detailed estimate of how much ice it has lost in recent decades.
Using satellite altimetry data covering 2002 to 2023, they found that the ice sheet lost an average of about 120 gigatonnes (264.5 trillion lbs) of mass per year.
This figure is considerably lower than the widely cited figure reached by Nasa, which previously estimated Greenland’s annual loss to be nearly 270...
title: Why China’s new estimate on Greenland ice loss speed is 55% lower than America’s

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
Brazilian leader Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva staged a surprise comeback to secure a fourth term in office, extending a presidency that has overseen deepening ties with China and sporadic clashes with the United States.
With almost all of the ballots in Sunday’s presidential run-off counted, Lula led with 51.8 per cent of the votes to 48.2 per cent for Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. The 80-year-old left-winger is the first person to win the presidency after losing the first round of voting since Brazil...
title: Lula secures surprise win to retain Brazil presidency

author: Alcott Wei
description:
The Communist Party has started a key four-day conclave focused on party discipline and fighting corruption, as official media outlets say adherence to the party’s leadership under President Xi Jinping is key to the country’s success.
The meeting – the fifth plenum of the Communist Party’s 20th Central Committee – began in Beijing on Monday, according to state news agency Xinhua.
It said the main agenda for the plenum included a work report by the Politburo to the Central Committee and the...
title: China’s Communist Party opens fifth plenum with focus on discipline and loyalty to Xi

author: Carol Yang
description:
An AI-generated Chinese rap song featuring some of the country’s most well-known historical figures has taken social media by storm.
Titled “The One Who’s Been There” (Guo Lai Ren), the track crossed 100 million views across platforms in less than two weeks as it tapped into the anxieties of modern life.
The song brings together 10 iconic figures from Chinese history and mythology – from revered poets and statesmen to the legendary Monkey King. Rather than reciting classical verses or lecturing...
title: 100 million views: why China’s viral AI rap track has struck a chord

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese researchers have found that the Yarlung Tsangpo River – soon to host the largest mega dam in the world – may face increased run-off and flood risks over this century.
Using tree-ring width chronologies in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, the team reconstructed the river’s run-off history from 1325 to 2020.
Along with climate data, this was used to create a model that projected river run-off would increase under future climate scenarios, along with a possible increase in high-run-off...
title: Tibetan river hosting world’s biggest dam is facing increasing flood risk: study

author: William Zheng
description:
North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s tour of a commercial vehicle factory during a surprise visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday points to Pyongyang’s drive to modernise its buses and expand industrial ties with Beijing.
In a symbolic move, Kim crossed into China via the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge on Saturday and also returned to North Korea via the bridge later in the day.
It was Kim’s first trip to China since he attended a military parade in Beijing last September. His...
title: Why North Korean leader Kim Jong-un toured a Chinese bus factory in Dandong

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won re-election on Sunday in a dramatic comeback after trailing in the first round, extending the rule of a government that has overseen record Chinese investment.
The Superior Electoral Court said Lula had 51.76 per cent of valid votes against 48.24 per cent for right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, with 99.83 per cent votes counted. No candidate who trailed after the first round had won a run-off since Brazil adopted the system in 1989.
But the...
title: Lula pulls off Brazil’s first-ever run-off comeback to beat Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro
